audience.audience: Engineers and technical leads building or evaluating agents; ordinary language before SideFX vocabulary.
audience.seriesPromise: One agent claim, one visible check, one bounded conclusion.
audience.demandTheme: Trusting agent action and completion reports
audience.humanStake: People retain authority over consequential changes and can see unmet needs.
audience.curiosityQuestion: Which observed fact justifies this claim?
audience.intensityCurve: Conflict immediately; concentrate motion on counterexample and new fact; settle on usable report.
audience.payoff: Concrete report or handoff, with remaining uncertainty visible.
audience.shareHypothesis: A useful checklist may invite discussion among agent builders; unmeasured.
audience.evidenceStatus: Creative hypotheses only. No audience, retention, conversion or learning claims.

scenes.narration: Inspect candidate C seventeen. Do not publish it. The agent queues publication anyway. That would put an unreviewed change in front of users. Same candidate, different action. Before that command runs, what actually stops it?
scenes.direction: Brief engineer establishing shot, then cut into the exact requested and queued action. Focus moves from person to mismatched verb.

scenes.narration: Here is one frozen SideFX decision expression. For an adjudicate request, it compares the tool name with dangerous tool. A match returns operator required. Any other name returns allow. These are returned labels. Neither label, by itself, stops a command.

states.title: The check is a name test.

scenes.direction: Isolate input, comparison, returned string. No full circuit or activation badges; returned-label qualification has equal visual priority.

scenes.narration: Try an unrecognized name: publish alias. The expression still returns allow. Which checked fact establishes permission to publish? None. This counterexample breaks the claim that this name test establishes authorization. It does not demonstrate an escaped effect on a live platform.
scenes.direction: Keep operation fixed, replace only the name, then reveal the evaluated output. The observable result is local expression evaluation.

scenes.narration: Separate three responsibilities. The person requests an inspection. The organization grants inspection of C seventeen, with read only arguments. An operator may approve an exception only within delegated authority. Approval cannot create power the organization never delegated.
scenes.direction: Build the authority relationship before introducing dispatcher. Grant belongs outside the agent; no invented SCL altitude.

scenes.narration: The proposed dispatcher owns the effect credential. It checks the protected grant before dispatch. The agent cannot edit that grant or acquire the credential. Unavailable authorization means hold. This is the trust boundary to build and test, not evidence that SideFX already enforces it.
scenes.direction: A request trace reaches the dispatcher and stops there. The effect segment never lights up; diagram explicitly proposed.

scenes.narration: Now a deliberately small simulation. Publication reaches our dispatcher with an inspection only grant. It is held. A separate inspection of the same candidate is permitted. The dispatcher records these calls; the agent does not write that observation. This covers only this toy route.
scenes.direction: Two actual local toy calls, one denied publication then one allowed read. Values must match worked-evidence.json; no claim of managed execution.

scenes.narration: Open the returned report: two checks pass; one required summary is missing. The engineer now has something to repair. Candidate C seventeen remains unpublished. That is a useful inspection result, not a publication success and not a production security certification.
scenes.direction: Open a concrete report artifact; reveal missing summary and unchanged state. The payoff is knowledge, with no fabricated live recovery.

scenes.narration: Change the object to C eighteen, keeping the old grant. The dispatcher holds the request: the object no longer matches. Changing approved arguments must also invalidate the match. Permission belongs to the bound action, object, and arguments, not to a reassuring label.
scenes.direction: Replace object in request only; retain grant visibly. Freeze trace at mismatch; evidence comes from toy model.

scenes.narration: For a real boundary, observe the denied attempt at dispatch and the permitted inspection output in the same session. Match caller, object, arguments, and policy version. Then test another route. Our toy observer sees no shell or second adapter. Those paths remain unverified.
scenes.direction: Pair two observations, then expose a separate unobserved route. No animated traversal presented as execution or proof.

scenes.narration: Use the boundary evidence checklist: name the effect, bind the grant, locate the dispatcher, and test a changed condition. A permission label is not an off switch. Next, the tool succeeds. Can the agent truthfully say the task is complete?
scenes.direction: Land the tested distinction; sequel promise matches Episode 2 exactly. Hold CTA long enough to read.

source: Projection of JSON content store; edit the store.
